name: GA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Jack with large financial advantage
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Jack's incumbency and roughly 13-to-1 fundraising advantage over Maura Keller, and markets pricing a Republican win near 94% all point the same way. No polls or expert ratings exist, but the fundamentals leave little room for doubt.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention on Keller's behalf or a sudden polling surprise showing the race competitive would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 3rd District leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Brian Jack is running for reelection and has built a substantial war chest, raising over $2 million and holding more than $1.1 million on hand. Democratic challenger Maura Keller has raised only about $150,000, leaving her badly outmatched financially.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets price Jack's chances at roughly 94 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes this a Safe Republican seat, with Keller facing an uphill fight to even keep the margin close.
